part1.question: Do you work or are you a student?
hints: 先直接回答身份，不要绕弯子
补充专业或工作内容，给一个具体细节
可以加一句感受，让回答自然结束
part1.sample: I'm a final-year student majoring in environmental engineering. I spend a substantial part of my week in the lab, testing water samples, which I find surprisingly hands-on and rewarding.

part1.question: What do you like most about your hometown?
hints: 选一个具体的地点或生活方式
对比过去与现在，体现变化
用一个小例子支撑观点
part1.sample: What I like most is how easy it is to get around. The local government has invested in public transport, which has helped mitigate traffic congestion, although air quality in some districts has deteriorated over the years.

part1.question: Do you enjoy reading?
hints: 解释阅读带来的具体好处
可提纸质书与电子书的选择
part1.sample: Yes, I try to read for a substantial amount of time every evening. I mostly read non-fiction, because it gives me a wider perspective on how other people live and work.

part2.cueCard: Describe a place you visited that impressed you.
points: and explain why it impressed you
followUp: Would you like to go back there?
Do you prefer travelling alone or with others?
part2.sample: I'd like to talk about a riverside cultural centre I visited last spring. The venue was converted from an old warehouse, and the architects kept the original brick walls. What impressed me most was how the space brought local artists and residents together. A substantial part of the building is free to the public, so teenagers can study there after school. It made me realise that good design can change how a community uses a city.

part2.cueCard: Describe a time when you had to change your plans.
points: why you had to change it
and explain how you felt about the change
followUp: Do you usually make detailed plans?
How do you feel when plans change suddenly?
part2.sample: Last summer my friends and I planned a hiking trip, but the weather forecast was terrible, so we decided to postpone it. Instead, we spent the weekend in a small town nearby, visiting a museum and a local market. At first I was frustrated because I had booked the transport months in advance, but in the end the slower trip was more relaxing than the original plan.

part3.question: Why do some people prefer detailed plans while others prefer to be spontaneous?
hints: 从性格与安全感角度解释计划派
从灵活性、创造力和不可控因素解释随性派
part3.sample: Detailed planners often feel safer when they can anticipate problems, especially when money or other people are involved. Spontaneous people, on the other hand, may value flexibility and enjoy discovering things they could not have planned. In practice, most people postpone decisions when the risk is high and stay flexible when the cost of changing plans is low.

part3.question: How has technology changed the way people organise their time?
hints: 效率提升：日历、提醒、在线协作
边界模糊：工作与休息混在一起
part3.sample: Technology has made scheduling far more efficient: shared calendars and reminders save a substantial amount of time. But it has also blurred the boundary between work and rest, because people can be reached at almost any hour. So the benefit depends on whether individuals set clear limits.

part3.question: Should governments spend more money on public transport?
hints: 支持：减少拥堵与排放，提升可达性
质疑：建设成本高、郊区覆盖不足
part3.sample: I think they should, provided the investment is targeted. Better bus and rail networks can mitigate congestion and reduce emissions, and they give people without cars access to jobs. However, building in low-density areas is expensive, so governments should prioritise routes with real demand rather than announcing large projects for political reasons.
